importantFindings.reproduction: With synthetic rows, open the real current desktop database in a second page wrapped in that historical D3 guard with writer version 0.4.0. Import a same-ID course through the visible D4 preview, acknowledgement and replacement button, setting the selected student's initial note to 'imported replacement note'. The historical guard then successfully writes 'late D3 note' to that same ID; querying the real engine returns the late value. The 5.1-second audit test asserts this observed boundary, not successful stale-writer protection. It uses the exact historical guard with the current pinned real browser engine, not a complete historical application build.

Read the current D4 predicate, 0.4 local-only scope and Technical Decisions startup/lifecycle contract. The 193a250..ac0c255 application delta is confined to engineModuleCompiler.ts and its new producer tests; broker, cache promise sharing, deadlines, termination, SDK/VFS, database/schema, write guard and course generation are unchanged.

Inspected the new producer: validate the same-origin request, perform one fetch, require HTTP ok and exact ASCII case-insensitive application/wasm MIME with HTTP whitespace trimming, await the complete ArrayBuffer, then construct one immutable WebAssembly.Module inside the existing code-only worker. Fetch/body/constructor exceptions retain the existing error reply. No WebAssembly.Instance, database, backend, extra retry or warm-up is added.

Independent targeted verification: npx vitest run src/persistence/engineModuleCompiler.test.ts src/persistence/engineModuleBroker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1; 2 files, 20 tests PASS. Includes concurrent opens sharing compilation, fresh SDK worker ownership, one failed consumer preserving the surviving compilation, compile failures, timeout termination/retry, response rejection and malformed diagnostic metadata.

Six independent production-mode producer probes PASS in Node VM with real WebAssembly.Module and synthetic minimal WASM: exactly one immutable module with no Instance or diagnostic clock reads; fetch interruption reported once without retry; body interruption before compilation; unresolved body unable to construct or announce a module; failed HTTP status rejected before body access; non-ASCII MIME lookalike rejected. Source was TypeScript-transpiled with DEV=false. Initial scratch assertions incorrectly assumed same-realm object/error prototypes; only that probe harness was corrected. Scratch script/results are OS temporary cvc-d4-sync-review-round2-producer.mjs and cvc-d4-sync-review-round2-producer-results.json.

Inspected .evidence/D4/ci-worker-compile-probe.json as diagnostic evidence only: four fresh macOS jobs, 32 original D1 cases PASS without retries; worker-sync opens 1118/1394 ms and streaming opens 1313/4789 ms; 609 rows, 40 injected students, 520 evaluations and identical reopening retained. This comparison does not establish a causal fix or replace exact canonical CI.
